title: TensorGuard: Static Tensor Shape Verification for PyTorch

reviewers.name: Yuan Cheng
reviewers.key_strength: Fragment-aware decidability classification provides honest uncertainty reporting, a rare and valuable trait in verification tooling.
reviewers.key_weakness: Confidence calibration is fundamentally underspecified — no ECE, calibration curves, or power analysis to support the zero-false-positive claim.

reviewers.name: Aniruddha Sinha
reviewers.key_strength: CEGAR loop with Houdini-style predicate accumulation and O(k) convergence is a clean, well-executed adaptation of mature verification techniques.
reviewers.key_weakness: IC3/PDR is compared only against bounded checking, not k-induction or interpolation; CEGAR and IC3/PDR are offered as independent modes rather than unified.

reviewers.name: Lila Zhang
reviewers.key_strength: Knuth-Bendix completion with provably confluent TRS and Lean 4 mechanization of individual propagator specs demonstrate strong formal foundations.
reviewers.key_weakness: CrossTheoryDeductionPropagator soundness is not mechanized, leaving the most critical gap between per-theory and system-level formal guarantees.

reviewers.name: Sara Roy
reviewers.key_strength: TorchBench evaluation on 33 real-world models with 222ms average and CLI/SARIF/CI integration demonstrates strong practical deployment readiness.
reviewers.key_weakness: Benchmark results are not stratified by difficulty or architecture family, making it impossible to assess performance on complex shape dynamics.

reviewers.name: Joseph S. Chang
reviewers.key_strength: Proof certificate architecture with four cascading strategies and 100% coverage sets a standard that other domain-specific verification tools should emulate.
reviewers.key_weakness: System-level composition theorem for the 5-theory product domain is not mechanized in Lean 4, and proof certificate format lacks standardization (e.g., Alethe/LFSC).

consensus_strengths: Comprehensive verification infrastructure combining IC3/PDR, CEGAR, assume-guarantee, and proof certificates into a cohesive, practically deployable system
Lean 4 mechanization with zero sorry obligations for individual theory propagators provides machine-checked trust in core reasoning components
Fragment-aware decidability classification honestly reports solver limitations rather than silently producing unsound results
Practical deployment readiness with CLI, SARIF output, GitHub Actions integration, and sub-second analysis times on real-world TorchBench models
consensus_weaknesses: System-level soundness of the 5-theory product domain composition is not formally established — CrossTheoryDeductionPropagator and combination theorem lack mechanized proofs
Statistical evaluation lacks rigor: no confidence intervals on F1, no calibration analysis for the confidence model, no power analysis for the zero-false-positive claim
Benchmark results are not stratified by difficulty tier or architecture family, obscuring performance on complex shape dynamics vs. simple linear chains
IC3/PDR is compared only against bounded checking, not natural competitors like k-induction or interpolation-based verification
Confidence model uses basic logistic regression (AUC-ROC=0.78) when modern ML-guided verification techniques could substantially improve uncertainty quantification
actionable_recommendations: Extend Lean 4 mechanization to cover the 5-theory composition theorem, including CrossTheoryDeductionPropagator soundness and interaction with Z3's DPLL(T) core
Stratify benchmark results by difficulty tier (sequential, DAG, attention/transformer, dynamic/conditional) and report per-category F1 with Wilson confidence intervals
Compare IC3/PDR against k-induction and interpolation-based approaches; unify IC3/PDR and CEGAR into a single verification strategy with CEGAR-based invariant strengthening
Replace logistic regression confidence model with a calibrated hierarchical model conditioned on SMT fragment class; report ECE, calibration curves, and high-confidence verdict fraction
Adopt a standardized proof certificate format (Alethe or LFSC) verifiable by an independent proof checker, and implement incremental Knuth-Bendix re-completion for operator extensibility
